title: Task / job scheduler (delayed, recurring, prerequisites; ScheduledExecutor-style)
prompt: Build an in-process scheduler: add a task (run at time T / after delay / every N / with priority or prerequisite tasks), get or run the next due task, complete or cancel it. Senior follow-up: run due tasks on a pool of worker threads safely (ScheduledExecutorService from scratch).
followups: make it thread-safe with N worker threads; sleep until next due time (DelayQueue / condition variable), wake early when an earlier task arrives
recurring / fixed-rate vs fixed-delay tasks; cancel a scheduled task
prerequisites -> valid completion order (topological sort), detect cycles (Brex milestone 3, Rippling DAG follow-up)
priorities + fairness; retry and timeout of a task; exception in a task must not kill the worker (Rubrik thread-pool follow-ups)
match jobs to machines by required capability (Microsoft)
batch/flush: run tasks once 10 accumulate or on flush() (Netflix TaskProcessor)
notes: Most frequent concurrency-flavoured LLD with no page among the 34 (blocking-queue and producer-consumer are its building blocks). Codezym tags: Design a Job Scheduler (microsoft, salesforce), Cron Job Scheduler (amazon). LC 7646238 claims 'ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor from scratch asked by Uber, GS, Rubrik' but it is a tutorial post (secondary). Also appears as CodeSignal ICF 'Task Management System' (Airbnb, Coinbase on fastprep).

title: Time-based / versioned key-value store (get at timestamp, snapshots, time travel)
prompt: Key-value store where every set creates a version: get(key) returns latest, get(key, timestamp or version) returns the value as of that point; later levels add snapshots / iterate a consistent snapshot, deletes, TTL, and concurrent readers.
followups: global version counter vs per-key timestamps; binary search over versions
delete as a tombstone version; get-at-time after delete
snapshot(): return an id; iterate the snapshot while writes continue (Databricks 'Snapshot Set Iterator')
historical field lookup inside CodeSignal ICF in-memory DB / banking 'balance at time T'
notes: inmem-db covers transactions, not version history. fastprep: Oracle 'Time-Based Key-Value Store' 3 reports; Ramp 'In-Memory DB with TTL and Historical Lookup' 5; Lyft 'Globally Versioned KV' 1; Databricks 'Snapshot Set Iterator' 2; Meta 'In-Memory DB with Historical Field Lookup' 1; Coinbase 'Banking System with Historical Snapshots' 1. The caller's 'Databricks-like KV with snapshots' lead lands here.

title: Hit counter / sliding-window request counter (+ thread-safe, + QPS metrics)
prompt: Record hits (or GET/PUT calls) with timestamps and answer 'how many in the last N seconds/5 minutes' or 'average QPS'; follow-ups: configurable window, millions of hits per second, many threads calling hit() at once.
followups: bucketed circular array (O(window) memory) vs queue of timestamps
thread-safety: per-bucket atomics vs one lock
measure_put_load()/measure_get_load() = average calls per second over last 5 min on a KV map (Databricks)
notes: Codezym 'Hit Counter - Multi-Threaded' (q6) tagged amazon, adobe, atlassian, salesforce, microsoft, apple, uber, oracle; 'Configurable Time Window Hit Counter' (q403) similar tags. Apple fastprep 'Implement Hit Counter' 2 reports. Dropbox evidence is old (GitHub prep list).

title: O(1) insert / delete / getRandom store (RandomizedSet family, + generics, + concurrency)
prompt: Registry class with insert, delete, lookup and getRandom all O(1) average (app store, KV store, queue with getRandom). Interviewers then add duplicates, generic key/value types, or thread-safety.
followups: support duplicates (map value -> set of indices)
make it generic (template class) - Uber LLD round
enqueue/dequeue + getRandom (Confluent) then make it thread-safe
notes: LeetCode 380/381-style but asked inside LLD/coding rounds with class-design and concurrency follow-ups.

title: Meeting-room / slot booking scheduler (rooms, capacity, audit log, concurrency)
prompt: Given N rooms (with capacity), book a meeting [start,end) into a free room or return INVALID; list bookings; slots with a max booking count; follow-ups on capacity, best-fit room, and concurrent booking of the same slot.
followups: room capacity constraint; choose room that minimises idle 'spillage' (best fit)
store per-room audit logs and delete them after X days (Uber)
multithreaded booking of the same slot / held-but-not-paid slots (Amazon slot reservation)
recurring meetings; list bookings per room/user (codezym variants)
court booking: assign to first available court or open a new one (Atlassian DS round)
notes: bookmyshow covers seat booking, not interval-in-room booking. Codezym tags meeting-room scheduler to salesforce, uber, amazon. Google fastprep 'Restaurant Waitlist' and Pinterest 'restaurant seating windows' (LC 5526021) are adjacent.

title: File-API practical tasks: cp, tail -n, chunked read/write, directory size (often multithreaded)
prompt: Using only a small file interface (open/read(offset,len)/write/append/list), implement cp, tail(file, n), total directory size, delete-tree or a chunked reader; follow-up: parallelise with threads while keeping writes ordered and memory bounded.
followups: read in parallel chunks, merge, and minimise writes (SSD writes are costly) - Rubrik
files larger than RAM: stream, do not load (Confluent)
directory size with cached aggregates when files change
notes: file-system slug is an in-memory tree (mkdir/ls/cat/mv); these rounds test I/O against a given low-level API. Confluent recruiters describe the round as 'a practical problem involving files, low-level file access'.

title: Snake game (Nokia snake: board, food, growth, score)
prompt: Simulate snake on an R x C board: move(direction) returns score or -1 on self/wall collision; food list consumed in order grows the snake. Clean OOD + runnable code + tests.
followups: ask about boundary behaviour (wrap vs die)
print head and tail positions to console (Atlassian)
extensible: obstacles, multiple food types, speed levels
O(1) collision check with deque + hash set
notes: Not snake-ladder. Codezym q202 tags google, microsoft, meta, salesforce, uber, atlassian.

title: Popularity tracker / All-O(1) counter (increase, decrease, most popular, top-K)
prompt: increasePopularity(id), decreasePopularity(id), getMostPopular() (and least) in O(1); follow-ups: change by x instead of 1, tie-breaking, top-K printing.
followups: +x / -x updates break the O(1) bucket list -> ordered map of count -> set
tie-breaker: most recent vs smallest id
notes: At Atlassian this sits in the 'Data Structures' round next to Code Design; it is the coding form of the Tagging/popular-tags HLD question.

title: Leaderboard with live score updates (top-K, rank of a player)
prompt: Players/teams get score updates; return top-K and a player's rank; model games, players and scoring rules.
followups: rank closest to mine (Amazon 'chess in-memory DB' list item)
notes: fastprep: Pinterest 'Escape Room Leaderboard' 3 reports; Coinbase 'Dynamic Fixed-K Score Leaderboard' 1. Codezym 'Leaderboard for Fantasy Teams' (uber, microsoft).

title: Card games OOD (deck, Blackjack, combos, Camel Cards)
prompt: Model cards, deck, hands, players and winner rules for a card game (Blackjack or custom 3-card combos); shuffle multiple decks; rank hands.
followups: custom winner-checking rules as pluggable strategies
interviewer wanted OOD, not a quick set-based check (Amazon phone screen)
notes: Covers the caller's 'Amazon deck of cards' lead: seen as Amazon phone-screen OOD in 2024. fastprep: Rippling 'Camel Cards' 4 reports; Pinterest LLD 'Blackjack Table Game'.

title: Delivery cost tracker / driver payroll (Rippling) and Dasher pay (DoorDash)
prompt: addDriver(id, hourlyRate), addDelivery(driverId, start, end); total cost of all deliveries; payUpToTime(t) and getTotalUnpaid(); analytics like max simultaneous drivers in last 24h. DoorDash: compute dasher pay from pickup/dropoff events with a multiplier per concurrent order.
followups: money precision (cents / BigDecimal; rate per second)
payUpToTime must not double-pay; make it faster than O(n) (binary search / prefix sums)
max simultaneous drivers in last 24h (sweep line)
DoorDash: store waits and peak-hour multipliers; call an upstream payments API
notes: fastprep: Rippling 'Delivery Cost Tracker' 13 reports (its most reported question), plus 'with Effective-Dated Rates' 2 and 'Driver Balance Ledger' 1; DoorDash 'Dasher Pay with Store Waits and Peak Hours' 7.

title: Employee directory / access management (grant, revoke, inherit through org tree)
prompt: Model employees, managers, teams; grant(resource, employee), revoke, hasAccess with inheritance through the hierarchy; hierarchical view from any employee.
followups: cap org-tree height h: anyone deeper reports to the CEO (Rippling)
closest common group for a set of employees (Atlassian DS round)
notes: fastprep: Rippling 'Employee Resource Access Management' 3, 'Limit an Organization Tree's Height' 1. Atlassian's 'employee hierarchy / closest group' is a Data Structures question (LC 7021261, 7246118).

title: Car / bike rental (inventory + reservations)
prompt: Search available vehicles by type/location/time, reserve, pick up, return, bill; car inventory service + reservation service.
followups: searchBikes with list of filters + location (Salesforce)
overlapping reservations for the same car
notes: Codezym q21 'Car Rental System' tags amazon, uber.

title: Library management / checkout
prompt: Titles vs physical copies, members, checkout/return/reserve, fines; sometimes plus DB schema and SQL.
followups: write the SQL for overdue books (Bloomberg)
notes: Microsoft fastprep LLD 'Design a Library Circulation System'.

title: Inventory / order processing with concurrency and idempotency
prompt: Reserve stock for orders across warehouses, handle concurrent orders for the last unit, process an order exactly once even when the same order arrives twice (retries).
followups: two buyers, one unit: lock granularity
idempotency key for duplicate order messages
notes: Codezym q4 'order and inventory management - Multi-Threaded' tags intuit, amazon (and India companies).

title: Online auction / bidding system
prompt: Create auctions, place bids with validation, close at end time, pick winner; extensible rules.
followups: requirements revealed as follow-ups to test extensibility (Amazon)
notes: Meta asks 'Instagram auction' as a Product Architecture (HLD) question, not LLD.

title: Autocomplete / search-suggestion engine (LLD)
prompt: Suggest top-K completions for a prefix from a dictionary or history (IDE keywords/methods/variables); ranking and updates.
notes: Often asked as DSA; Microsoft asks it as an LLD round.

title: Multithreaded web crawler
prompt: Given startUrl and an HtmlParser/fetch API, crawl all pages under the same host (or to max depth); then make it multithreaded without duplicate visits.
followups: stop condition when all workers idle
notes: Dropbox evidence is the community prep repo (pre-2023, 'EXTREMELY popular for onsite'). Atlassian's web-scraper questions are HLD rounds, not coding.

title: Thread-safe buffered / durable log writer (EventWriter, BufferedFileWriter, WAL batch writer)
prompt: Wrap a slow file API: many threads call append(bytes); batch writes into a buffer, flush on size/time, keep order, and guarantee durability (fsync) without fsync-per-call.
followups: producer-consumer between callers and a single writer thread
ordered writes with multiple writer threads
three threads: producer, framework, sink exchanging via a buffer (Microsoft logging framework)
notes: logger slug covers levels/appenders, not the concurrent durable-writer core. fastprep Databricks: 'Concurrent Buffered File Logger', 'Durable Data Writer', LLD 'WAL-Backed Batch Log Writer'.

title: Thread pool executor from scratch
prompt: Implement a fixed-size thread pool: submit(Runnable/Callable) -> Future, workers take from a bounded queue, shutdown/awaitTermination.
followups: exception in a task must not kill the worker
task timeout; reclaim a stuck thread
build it on your own bounded blocking queue (Rubrik)
fetch file chunks in parallel through the pool (Databricks CachedFile)
notes: Pairs with mt-blocking-queue (existing).

title: Composable iterators (interleave, range, list of iterators, filter, remove)
prompt: Part 1 zigzag over 2 arrays; part 2 range iterator(start,end,step); part 3 interleave a list of iterators; part 4 add filter(). Other variants: nested-list iterator with remove, lazy k-way union, snapshot set iterator.
notes: Coinbase's most repeated onsite coding theme in 2024 reports.

title: Records API: filters + cursor pagination (+ sorting)
prompt: Given transactions (id, user, currency, amount, time) implement query with multiple filters, limit, and next-cursor pagination; explain offset vs cursor.

title: Currency conversion (direct -> one hop -> best rate / path)
prompt: Parse 'USD:CAD:DHL:5,...' or rate pairs; convert amount with direct rate, then via at most one intermediate, then best rate / max-rate path with reconstruction.
followups: min-cost path with shipping method returned (Stripe)
notes: More DSA than LLD at Amazon/Uber (graph). fastprep: Amazon 'Currency Conversion Rate' 4, Rippling 'Maximum Currency Conversion Along a Simple Path' 2.

title: Rules / validation engine over records (fraud rules, KYC checks, expense policy, fees)
prompt: Multi-part: parse CSV/records, apply a growing list of rules (non-empty fields, amount ranges, behaviour-match %, expense caps), output decisions/reasons; rules should be data-driven.
notes: fastprep: Rippling 'Corporate Card Expense Rules' 9 reports; Stripe 'Business Account KYC Verification Parts 1-5' 7, 'Transaction Fee Calculator' 3, 'Rule-Driven Transaction Fraud Detection' 2, 'Evaluate Ordered Action Rules' 2; Ramp 'Detect Recurring Transactions' 1.

title: Load balancer / request router simulation (round-robin, weighted, sticky, consistent hashing)
prompt: Simulate routing of requests/WebSocket connections to servers with parts that add weights, TTL, sticky sessions, draining; or debug broken round-robin and consistent-hashing routers.
notes: Aggregator-only evidence: fastprep Stripe OA 'WebSocket Load Balancer Parts 1-5' 9 reports, 'Request Routing System' 8, onsite 'Weighted Server Load Balancer with TTL' 2; DoorDash project 'Debug Two Routing Strategies' (codezym DoorDash 'Debugging: Round Robin Traffic Router').

title: Priority waitlist queue (Genius Bar VIP queue, restaurant waitlist)
prompt: Customers join a queue (regular vs VIP / party size); serve by priority rules with fairness; estimate wait.
notes: fastprep Google 'Restaurant Waitlist' 2 reports; Intuit fastprep 'VIP-Priority Fixed-Window Rate Limiter' is a sibling.

title: CodeSignal ICF: cloud file storage (4 levels)
prompt: L1 add/copy/get file size; L2 top-N largest files by prefix; L3 users with storage capacity, merge users; L4 backup and restore (or compression).
followups: all state in memory; 90 minutes total
notes: fastprep: Airbnb 'Cloud Storage with User Backup and Restore' 3 + 'In-Memory File System' 2; Ramp 'Cloud Storage System Parts 1-4' 2 + 'Compression and Decompression' 3; Meta project 'In-Memory Cloud Storage System'. Different from file-system slug (flat paths, users, quotas, backups).

title: CodeSignal ICF: worker management (register, top workers, promotions/overtime, merge)
prompt: L1 register workers and office check-ins/outs; L2 top workers by time; L3 promotions with salary changes or overtime rules; L4 double-pay intervals or merge workers.
followups: salary changes effective at a timestamp
notes: Aggregator-only: fastprep Airbnb 3 reports per part, Ramp 5, Instacart 1.

title: Middleware / URL router with wildcards and path params (Atlassian)
prompt: addRoute(pattern, result); callRoute(path) returns the best match. '*' matches exactly one segment; ':id' captures a param. Variant: KV get/put where get supports wildcards.
followups: trie by path segment (interviewer may insist on a trie)
capture path params in the result

title: Customer-support agent rating leaderboard (Atlassian 'Customer Satisfaction')
prompt: giveRating(agent, 1..5); getRatings() returns agents by average rating desc; then best agents per month; export.
followups: getRatings called often -> keep sorted structure instead of sorting each call
notes: Atlassian's most reported Code Design question in 2025-26.

title: File collections size report (total size, top-N collections)
prompt: addFile(name, size, collections...); report total size of all files and top N collections by size; a file may belong to several collections.
notes: Atlassian Data Structures round / P60 phone screen.

title: Product plan / subscription cost explorer (Atlassian)
prompt: Customers subscribe to products on plans with prices; compute monthly/yearly cost; plan changes mid-period.
notes: Weak: one report ('some question around Subscription for different products'), codezym q38. Codezym also lists 'Last Lap Hero (F1 race tracker)' (q46) for Atlassian - no first-hand report found.

title: Unix find / grep as an API (filter specifications)
prompt: find(dir, criteria) for size > X, extension, name pattern; extensible criteria; follow-up AND/OR/NOT combinations. grep variant: case-insensitive, invert match, count, context lines.
followups: Specification / Composite pattern for boolean predicates
new filters without touching old code
notes: Also in Amazon question lists compiled from LC (LC 4688429 2024, 7060987 2025). Classic AWS 'logical and maintainable' question.

title: Amazon Locker (assign locker by package size, OTP pickup, expiry)
prompt: Lockers of sizes S/M/L at locations; assign smallest fitting free locker to a package, notify with code, customer opens with code, free locker after pickup or return after N days.
followups: concurrency: two packages grab the same locker
notes: Asked as 'logical and maintainable' coding (AWS Seattle 2024 bar raiser) and as LLD/HLD in India. Google fastprep 'Assign Locker' (2 reports) is a smaller cousin.

title: Pizza pricing / coffee machine (decorator + builder, deals)
prompt: Price a pizza from base + toppings (+ drinks, deals like BOGO); coffee machine with recipes; requirements arrive as follow-ups to test extensibility.
notes: LC 6566858 (2025) is a pizza-store LLD write-up attributed to Amazon.

title: Music player / song-play analytics (Rippling)
prompt: addSong(title) -> id; playSong(songId, userId); printAnalyticsSummary() by unique listeners; lastThreePlayedSongTitles(userId).
followups: star/unstar favourites + last N favourites played
notes: fastprep Rippling 'Song Play Analytics' 8 reports. Salesforce asked an 'LLD of Spotify' (2026). Atlassian asks 'top-k songs by number of users' as DSA (LC 6959323).

title: Shipping cost calculator (Stripe, tiered pricing parts 1-3)
prompt: Given an order (country, product, quantity) and a shipping-cost config, compute cost: part 1 fixed per-unit, part 2 volume tiers, part 3 mixed fixed/incremental tiers.
notes: fastprep: 12 reports (Stripe's top phone-screen item).

title: Invoice / payment reconciliation (Stripe)
prompt: Match payments to invoices from parsed input; report paid, partially paid, unmatched.
notes: Aggregator-only: fastprep 9 reports (phone screen).

title: Subscription email / invoice notification scheduler (Stripe)
prompt: Given customers with plans and a schedule of events (welcome, upcoming renewal, expired, invoice due, delinquent), print the emails to send in time order; later parts add plan changes.
notes: Aggregator-only: fastprep 'Email Subscription Scheduler' 12 onsite reports, 'Schedule Invoice Emails and Delinquencies' 2 (2023).

title: HTTP Accept-Language matching (Stripe)
prompt: parse(header, supported) returns supported tags in preference order; parts add language-only prefixes ('en' matches en-US), '*' wildcard, and q-factors.
followups: stable ordering by q then header position
notes: fastprep 4 reports.

title: Account balance manager / rebalance accounts to a minimum (Stripe)
prompt: Process transfers between accounts, compute totals, reject overdrafts; keep every account above a threshold with minimal transfers.
notes: fastprep 'Account Balance Manager Parts 1-3' 4 reports; 'Rebalance Bank Accounts' 1.

title: Aggregate several mocked services into one API response (DoorDash Code Craft)
prompt: Implement an endpoint that calls 2-3 mocked downstream services (profile, orders, payments), merges fields into one JSON, handles failures/timeouts.
notes: fastprep 'Customer Bootstrap API' 5 reports; DoorDash AI Code Craft (LC 7401147, 2025) instead gives an existing refund codebase: make the test pass, add partial refunds, then refactor.

title: Crypto price dashboard (averages across exchanges)
prompt: Token prices arrive every 2s from several exchanges; show per-token average/trend refreshed every 10s.

title: Fractional share inventory (Robinhood)
prompt: Customers buy/sell fractional shares or dollar amounts; firm buys whole shares from the exchange and keeps inventory in [0,1) per symbol.

title: Circular buffer + streamed log/query matcher (Datadog)
prompt: Implement a fixed-size circular FIFO buffer; separately, stream of 'Q:' queries and 'L:' logs - match each log to earlier queries whose words it contains.
notes: Datadog coding rounds run your code against tests.

title: Train platform management (Uber)
prompt: Assign arriving trains to free platforms, queue when none free, release on departure; strategies (min-heap earliest-free vs random).

title: Multi-level EV charging station (Microsoft)
prompt: Chargers of different types across levels; assign vehicles, billing strategies.

title: Pluggable data-access layer / DB SDK (Microsoft)
prompt: Data retrieval/update where the source (DB, API, file) can change at runtime; or a client SDK supporting several databases and auth mechanisms.

title: Feature flag / rollout evaluator
prompt: Define flags with targeting rules and percentage rollout; evaluate per user.
notes: Microsoft L60 candidate rejected on it; Google fastprep project 'Docs Mobile Feature Rollout' (repair an evaluator).

title: Salesforce signature LLDs: watch party, service-dependency impact analyzer, workflow state history
prompt: Watch party: host creates room, users join by id, synchronized play/pause/seek. Impact analyzer: given microservice dependency graph, blast radius and depth of a failure, cycles. Workflow: log and query step state transitions.
notes: India MTS/SMTS loops, HackerRank working code.

title: Nutanix LLDs: paint application, bookmarks manager, airport runway
prompt: Paint app with shapes/tools/undo (running code in 1 hour); manage bookmarks across browsers; runway scheduling for arrivals (fuel limits) and departures.

title: Rubrik concurrency classics: search-insert-delete list, exclusive team room, page cache
prompt: (1) Linked list shared by searchers (concurrent), inserters (exclusive among inserters) and deleters (exclusive with all). (2) Playground usable by one team at a time, max 10 players. (3) Logical memory unit that fetches pages from physical memory - make thread-safe.
notes: Search-insert-delete is the 'Little Book of Semaphores' problem; the playground is the unisex-bathroom pattern (closest existing pages: mt-rwlock, mt-h2o).

title: Lock/unlock nodes in a tree (ancestors and descendants must be unlocked)
prompt: lock(node)/unlock(node)/upgrade with parent pointers; optionally thread-safe.

title: Generic connection / resource pool
prompt: Borrow/return pooled resources of any kind (DB connections, threads) with max size, timeouts, validation.
notes: Rippling's is a vaguer 'Resource Manager' (add/remove/manage resources).

title: Circuit breaker around an RPC
prompt: Wrap an rpc method: closed -> open after N failures -> half-open probe -> closed.

title: Other Amazon LLD prompts seen once (2024-2026)
prompt: Restaurant, cache system, offline download manager, event logging, device-related LLD, monitoring/alerting from metric streams (L6), storefront search/filter, GoodReads.
notes: Long tail; no single prompt repeats.

title: Rate limiter (per user X requests in Y seconds)
prompt: rateLimit(customerId) -> bool for X requests per Y seconds; choose fixed window / sliding log / sliding window counter / token bucket.
followups: credits: unused requests carry over as credit (Atlassian)
multiple rules: global, per path, user+path, user+path+tenant (Cloudflare isRateLimited)
queue requests instead of rejecting - bounded token-bucket request queue (Plaid)

title: LRU / LFU cache and its variants
prompt: get/put O(1) with capacity eviction; variants add TTL, counters, custom eviction by an external rank, or thread-safety.
followups: LRU with TTL / expire after 5 min (Google, Confluent, Amazon)

LFU where access changes a score field (Google)
